summary: On 8 November 2026, Russia launched coordinated missile and drone attacks across multiple Ukrainian regions, with a Geran-5 missile striking the Cherkasy Thermal Power Plant and multiple reactive drones and Shahed drones reported in Chernihiv, Poltava, Kyiv, and other oblasts. Ukrainian air defense intercepted several threats while a Ukrainian tactical aviation strike destroyed a Russian logistics node containing ammunition and drones. The US is preparing a $15 billion military aid package for Ukraine, though Germany has stated its Patriot systems are exhausted.
key_points: A Geran-5 missile struck the Cherkasy Thermal Power Plant (TPP), with additional Geran-5 missiles reported targeting Cherkasy city at distances of 48 km and with 5-7 minutes flight time (Source: @mon1tor_ua/78057, @mon1tor_ua/78058, @mon1tor_ua/78059).

Multiple reactive drones and Shahed drones were detected across Chernihiv, Poltava, Kyiv, Mykolaiv, Vinnytsia, Sumy, and Kirovohrad regions, with specific flight paths toward cities including Slavutych, Poltava, Kremenchuk, and Aviatorske (Source: @kpszsu/94187, @kpszsu/94209, @kpszsu/94210, @kpszsu/94224, @kpszsu/94225).

Ukrainian air defense intercepted or shot down multiple threats including a reactive Shahed near Nivky, a Geran-5 in Khmelnytskyi, and reactive Shaheds over Brovary and Vinnytsia (Source: @mon1tor_ua/78041, @mon1tor_ua/78042, @mon1tor_ua/78052, @mon1tor_ua/78061).
The 39th Tactical Aviation Brigade of Ukraine destroyed a Russian logistics node containing ammunition, drones, and food, disrupting assault preparations (Source: @UkraineNow/85173).

A fire broke out at a Russian defense industry facility in Saint Petersburg, specifically the 'Scientific-Production Association of Special Materials' hangar covering 300 square meters, producing body armor and technical means for security forces (Source: @eRadarrua/129424).
Russian forces attacked emergency responders in Komyshuvakha, Zaporizhzhia oblast, damaging special rescue equipment after an initial aviation strike on a shelter (Source: @eRadarrua/129390).

The US is preparing a $15 billion military aid package for Ukraine including air defense interceptors, intelligence data, and Starlink support, requiring bipartisan support to overcome a presidential veto (Source: @UkraineNow/85178).
Germany has exhausted its capacity to transfer Patriot systems to Ukraine, with other nations expected to take over a larger share of air defense burden (Source: @UkraineNow/85177).

sections.executive_summary: On 8 November 2026, Russia launched coordinated missile and drone attacks across multiple Ukrainian regions, with a Geran-5 missile striking the Cherkasy Thermal Power Plant and multiple reactive drones and Shahed drones reported in Chernihiv, Poltava, Kyiv, and other oblasts. Ukrainian air defense intercepted several threats while a Ukrainian tactical aviation strike destroyed a Russian logistics node containing ammunition and drones. The US is preparing a $15 billion military aid package for Ukraine, though Germany has stated its Patriot systems are exhausted.

points: Ukrainian air defense forces were actively engaged across the country, with air raid alerts sounded in Kyiv, Chernihiv, Poltava, Cherkasy, Mykolaiv, Vinnytsia, Khmelnytskyi, Sumy, Kirovohrad, Rivne, and Lutsk regions throughout 8 November 2026. Multiple reactive drones and Shahed missiles were intercepted or shot down, including a Geran-5 missile that struck the Cherkasy TPP, causing significant infrastructure damage. The 39th Tactical Aviation Brigade successfully destroyed a Russian logistics node containing ammunition, drones, and food supplies, disrupting enemy assault preparations in the field.

Civilian infrastructure was targeted in multiple locations: a Geran-5 missile hit the Cherkasy Thermal Power Plant; reactive Shahed drones struck or crashed in Nivky (Kyiv), Brovary, and Vinnytsia; and a reactive Shahed fell on a shopping center in Berkivets. In Khmelnytskyi, a Geran-5 missile impacted in the South-Western/Dubove area. In Zaporizhzhia oblast, Russian forces attacked emergency responders at Komyshuvakha who were clearing debris from an earlier aviation strike on a shelter, damaging special rescue equipment. Power substations were also targeted, including one in Ovrut, Zhytomyr oblast, which was completely destroyed by drone strikes.

The Ukrainian government continued to coordinate air defense and civil protection measures. President Zelensky signed a decree on mandatory declaration for all Security Service of Ukraine (SBU) employees following an internal investigation into criminal cases involving violence. The Ministry of Internal Affairs was urged to resolve road blockages on the Mstislav road. Meanwhile, the Ukrainian tennis player Marta Kostyuk and Elina Svitolina advanced in the WTA Finals in Indian Wells, providing a morale boost amid ongoing hostilities.

Russian forces launched a massive wave of missile and drone attacks across Ukraine on 8 November 2026, employing Geran-5 missiles, cruise missiles (Banderol), and reactive Shahed drones. At least three Geran-5 missiles targeted Cherkasy city, with one striking the TPP at a distance of 48 km and a flight time of 5-7 minutes. Additional Geran-5 missiles were launched from Bryansk, Rovno, Zhytomyr, and Chernihiv oblasts toward targets in Kyiv, Chernihiv, Rivne, and Volyn regions. Multiple reactive Shahed drones were launched from Kharkiv, Mykolaiv, and the Black Sea toward Poltava, Vinnytsia, and the Mykolaiv-Odessa border.

A fire broke out at a Russian defense industry facility in Saint Petersburg on 8 November 2026, specifically at the Scientific-Production Association of Special Materials hangar covering 300 square meters. The facility produces body armor, engineering protection means, and technical counter-terrorism equipment for Russian security forces. The fire was localized with no immediate casualties reported. In a separate incident, Russian forces attacked Ukrainian emergency responders in Komyshuvakha, Zaporizhzhia oblast, damaging rescue equipment after an initial aviation strike on a civilian shelter.

Russia continued to prepare for assault operations, with a logistics node containing ammunition, drones, and food supplies destroyed by Ukrainian tactical aviation in the 39th Brigade's strike. Russian monitoring sources reported planned attacks on six bridges in Dnipro in the near future. Russia also sent a higher-level delegation to Abu Dhabi for peace talks with Ukraine, potentially indicating willingness for more substantive negotiations, though no breakthrough was reported.

In the Donbas region, Russian forces continued to prepare for assault operations, with Ukrainian tactical aviation destroying a logistics node containing ammunition, drones, and food supplies for troops preparing for storm actions. The 39th Tactical Aviation Brigade's strike led to the cancellation of individual assault operations by Russian forces. In Donetsk oblast, reactive drone groups were detected and monitored, with Ukrainian air defense actively engaging threats. The situation remained highly volatile with continued Russian attempts to advance in the area, though specific territorial changes were not reported in the available messages.

Russian forces in the eastern sector employed reactive drones and missiles to suppress Ukrainian positions and infrastructure. Multiple reactive drone groups were detected over Donetsk and Luhansk oblasts, with Ukrainian air defense intercepting several. The attacks on power infrastructure, including the Cherkasy TPP strike, were part of a broader campaign to degrade Ukraine's energy grid ahead of the winter period. Ukrainian forces maintained defensive positions and continued to receive Western military aid, including air defense systems and intelligence support, to counter the Russian offensive.

The northern front remained active with Russian drone and missile attacks targeting Chernihiv, Sumy, and Kyiv oblasts. Multiple reactive drones were detected over Chernihiv region, with flight paths toward Slavutych, Sedniv, Bereza, and Ladan/Lynovycha. In Sumy oblast, reactive drones and Banderol missiles were launched toward Duvazkivka, Nedyhailiv, and Romny. A Banderol missile was also detected flying over Novi Sanzhary in Poltava oblast, heading southeast.

Kyiv oblast experienced multiple threats including reactive drones flying near the Kyiv Reservoir toward Kyiv city, reactive Shahed drones falling in Nivky and targeting the Darnytskyi district, and Geran-5 missiles launched from Chernihiv oblast toward Vyshhorod district. Ukrainian air defense was actively engaged, with air raid alerts sounded in Kyiv and surrounding areas. The capital and northern regions continued to face regular drone and missile attacks, with civilian infrastructure and energy facilities remaining primary targets.

In the southern sector, Russian forces launched reactive drones from the Black Sea toward Mykolaiv oblast and the border with Odessa oblast. Multiple reactive drone groups were detected over Mykolaiv and Odessa regions, with Ukrainian air defense intercepting several. In Zaporizhzhia oblast, Russian forces attacked Ukrainian emergency responders at Komyshuvakha who were clearing debris from an earlier aviation strike on a civilian shelter, damaging special rescue equipment. No casualties among rescuers were reported.

Russian forces in the southern direction continued to employ drones and missiles to target Ukrainian infrastructure and defensive positions. The attacks on the Cherkasy TPP and other energy facilities were part of a broader campaign to degrade Ukraine's power grid before winter. Ukrainian forces in the south maintained defensive positions and received intelligence and air defense support from Western partners to counter the Russian offensive. The situation remained tense with continued Russian attempts to advance in the Zaporizhzhia and Kherson directions.

The air war over Ukraine intensified on 8 November 2026 with Russia launching coordinated missile and drone attacks across multiple regions. Ukrainian air defense forces were actively engaged, intercepting multiple Geran-5 missiles, cruise missiles (Banderol), and reactive Shahed drones. Specific intercepts included a Geran-5 missile over Khmelnytskyi, reactive Shahed drones over Nivky, Brovary, and Vinnytsia, and multiple drones over Chernihiv, Poltava, and Kyiv oblasts. Ukrainian air defense systems, including Patriot and other Western-provided systems, were operational but faced resource constraints.

Ukrainian tactical aviation conducted strikes against Russian targets, with the 39th Tactical Aviation Brigade destroying a logistics node containing ammunition, drones, and food supplies. This strike disrupted Russian assault preparations and demonstrated Ukraine's continued capability to conduct precision strikes. However, Germany announced it had exhausted its capacity to transfer additional Patriot systems to Ukraine, with other nations expected to take over a larger share of the air defense burden. The US was preparing a $15 billion military aid package including air defense interceptors and intelligence support to bolster Ukraine's air defense capabilities.

sections.threat_assessment: The threat environment remains highly volatile with Russia conducting coordinated missile and drone attacks across multiple Ukrainian regions. The Cherkasy TPP strike and attacks on power substations in Ovrut and other locations indicate a renewed focus on degrading Ukraine's energy infrastructure ahead of winter. Ukrainian air defense has been effective but faces resource constraints, particularly with Germany's Patriot systems exhausted and the US aid package still pending. The destruction of the Russian logistics node by Ukrainian tactical aviation demonstrates continued Ukrainian strike capability, but the attack on emergency responders in Zaporizhzhia highlights Russian targeting of civilian infrastructure and first responders. The fire at the Russian defense plant in Saint Petersburg suggests potential vulnerabilities in Russia's defense industrial base.
sections.regional_response: Western allies continue to support Ukraine with military aid, though the $15 billion US package faces legislative hurdles requiring Republican support to override a presidential veto. Germany's announcement that its Patriot systems are exhausted shifts the air defense burden to other nations, with the Contact Group on Defense of Ukraine scheduled to discuss this in mid-November. The Russian delegation's higher-level presence at Abu Dhabi talks suggests potential willingness for more substantive negotiations, though no breakthrough has been reported. Ukraine's domestic response includes continued air defense operations, civil protection measures, and internal security reforms following the SBU investigation.
sections.intelligence_notes: The pattern of Russian attacks suggests a multi-axis assault employing Geran-5 missiles, Banderol cruise missiles, and reactive Shahed drones from multiple launch points including Bryansk, Chernihiv, Kharkiv, Mykolaiv, and the Black Sea. Ukrainian air defense has demonstrated effectiveness but the loss of German Patriot capacity creates a potential gap. The Russian logistics node destruction indicates Ukrainian intelligence and strike capabilities are targeting enemy supply chains. The Saint Petersburg defense plant fire may indicate either accidents, sabotage, or collateral damage, but its impact on Russian body armor production requires monitoring. The US aid package's passage is critical for Ukraine's air defense and overall military capability through the winter period.
